cohort: The study included 12,501,183 vaginal births in the USA between January 2016 and December 2021, using birth-certificate data from the National Vital Statistics System.
finding: Racial and ethnic disparities in Obstetric Anal Sphincter Injury (OASI) persist regardless of parity, obstetric history, and mode of delivery, with Asian individuals consistently showing higher OASI hazards compared to White individuals, and higher rates observed among foreign-born residents in racial and ethnic minority groups.
mod_finding: OASI rates varied widely by mode of delivery (e.g., in primiparae, SVD 1.7%, OVD with forceps 14.8%, OVD with vacuum 6.6%), and while Asian primiparae had consistently higher OASI hazards irrespective of mode, other racial groups showed inconsistent associations depending on the mode of delivery.
gest_age: Gestational age was used as a timescale in the Cox proportional hazard regression models.
